commands: agent understand --target lib/binding_rust --mission 'what executes when Parser::parse runs, and what does a change to lib/src/parser.c put at risk?'
atlas_n_mission.challenge: what executes when the Rust binding's Parser::parse runs, and what does a change to lib/src/parser.c put at risk?
atlas_n_mission.answer: Parser::parse -> Parser::parse_with_options (DERIVED); parse_with_options -> ts_parser_parse_with_options UNRESOLVED; Atlas_N held no record of any function declared in an extern block (0 of 165) and no component for any C or header file: impact on lib/src/parser.c was refused (no censused component). Atlas_N did not invent a callee; it could not say that the path crosses into C or that C exists.
understanding_gaps: foreign modules were skipped by the extractor by design (R4.3 minimum set) -- neither claimed nor fabricated, but silently absent from the world model
include!("./bindings.rs") at item position was not followed by the path resolver, so ffi:: paths could not reach the declarations even if they existed
63 C/H files (and Zig, Go, Swift, Python) were in the inventory as UNKNOWN but in no component and no gap: the pilot saw a Rust/JS repository

differential.oracle: ground truth from the source: bindings.rs extern blocks and the C definitions in lib/src/**/*.c (ORACLE_READ by pattern match, recorded under manual_reads); tree-sitter is a parser, not a code-intelligence tool, so the differential is Atlas against source, not against the donor's own answers

implementation.mechanism_vs_implementation: tree-sitter's implementation (a C runtime behind bindgen output) is not absorbed; the mechanism studied is the language boundary itself, and the capability absorbed is Atlas seeing the Rust side of any extern boundary: FOREIGN_FUNCTION declarations with their ABI, calls resolved to them, include! splicing, and unrecognized source as a stated gap
changes: adapter extractor: extern blocks emit FOREIGN_FUNCTION identity and signature (block ABI, no body, DECLARATION role) and declared statics
adapter resolver: foreign functions bound as call targets; item-position include!("literal") splices the file into the including module; computed include! not followed
implementation.falsification: 7 mutants killed (foreign items not bound, include not spliced, include path from the crate root, foreign function as a definition, block ABI dropped, recognized files counted, computed include followed)

n_vs_n_plus_1.what_atlas_n_saw: a Rust/JS/TS repository; Parser::parse ending in an unresolved call
n_vs_n_plus_1.what_atlas_n_missed: 165 foreign entry points, the call path into C, and 171 files it has no frontend for
n_vs_n_plus_1.what_atlas_n_plus_1_sees: every C entry point the binding declares, 156 of them with resolved Rust callers; the parse path ends at a named FFI boundary; the unrecognized C/H/Zig/Go/Swift/Python files stated by extension
n_vs_n_plus_1.still_unknown: what the C does (no C frontend); method calls on raw FFI pointers and std iterators; resource acquisition and release across the boundary (ts_parser_new / ts_parser_delete)
